Paper Name: Modeling downdraft biomass gasification process by restricting chemical reaction equilibrium with Aspen Plus
NOTES: This paper is about biomass gasification process modeling using Aspen Plus. It does NOT report a hybrid renewable energy system (PV/WT/FC/H2/DG) with economic parameters like LCOE, COE, capital costs, O&M costs, etc. Most requested parameters are not applicable to this paper. The paper focuses on syngas composition, gasification temperature, equivalence ratio, and moisture content effects. No load demand, no LCOE/COE, no generator configurations (PV/WT/FC/EL/DG), no cost parameters, no component lifetimes, no system configuration counts. The paper reports: gasification temperature range 500-1000°C (recommended 650-800°C), ER range 0.2-0.45 (recommended 0.2-0.3), moisture content <10% recommended, biomass feedstock is hardwood chips with 25% initial moisture (8.91% after pre-drying), HHV=18.58 MJ/kg, bulk density=222.15 kg/m3, gasifier diameter=35.6cm, length=118.3cm, flow rate=65 m3/h (at 0°C, 101.3 kPa), carbon conversion rate 96-99%, cyclone efficiency 85%, LHV of syngas ~4.86-5.14 MJ/Nm3. Ultimate analysis: C=49.817%, H=5.556%, O=43.425%, N=0.078%, S=0.005%, Ash=1.119%. Proximate analysis: Volatile Matter=79.85%, Fixed Carbon=19.031%, Ash=1.119%. LHV of H2=11.2 MJ/Nm3, CO=13.1 MJ/Nm3, CH4=37.1 MJ/Nm3. Aspen Plus V7.3 used. IDEAL property method. HCOALGEN and DCOALIGT models for biomass enthalpy and density.
H2_LHV: 33.3 kWh/kg (119.88 MJ/kg) [NOTE: paper reports LHV of H2 as 11.2 MJ/Nm3, not in kWh/kg. Standard conversion gives ~33.3 kWh/kg but paper does not report this directly]
